title: arXiv AI papers — 19 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred relevance-first shortlist, not a popularity ranking; reliable attention/citation evidence is sparse for this new batch.

sections.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
sections.abstract: Introduces a research-agent framework that evolves evidence-grounded hypotheses into executable investigations, then learns from assessments and failures; the authors report gains across four life-science domains.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce DiscoveryRSI and DFM-Bench; their abstract reports hypothesis-quality scores rising from 4.86 to 5.39 after two self-improvement rounds and a 6.3% correspondence rate with later-published hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe human assessments as preliminary, and the reported evaluation is limited to four life-science domains; the abstract does not establish general research capability.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Evaluates hypothesis quality and research progress across four domains, includes preliminary expert review, and reports code availability; substance/relevance signals rather than measured readership.

sections.title: Self-Building Labs
sections.abstract: Proposes an agentic laboratory system that builds missing layouts, digital twins, robot skills, and workflows from a scientific goal, with demonstrations across robot setups and a quantum-dot synthesis experiment.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim their system can configure and extend lab capabilities from high-level objectives, and report a real-world quantum-dot synthesis as an end-to-end validation.
sections.unique_caveat: The real-world validation highlighted in the abstract is one synthesis experiment; multi-robot scaling is described, but broad transfer across scientific tasks is not established there. The project materials also retain human oversight and stop controls.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad AI/robotics/multiagent cross-listing and an end-to-end physical experiment distinguish it from simulation-only agent proposals; project site provides system details.

sections.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
sections.abstract: Presents SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 SEER-based medical studies, and agents for reproducing their claims and testing whether reasonable analytical alternatives change conclusions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report reproducing 77.4% of atomic claims and flagging 9.5% of fully reproduced findings for expert review as potentially sensitive to analytical choices.
sections.unique_caveat: The study is bounded to 20 SEER-based papers; the authors identify unavailable data as a major reproduction barrier and keep expert review central to judging whether flagged alternatives are consequential.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-lists AI and language research, with concrete evaluation scale of 2,190 atomic claims plus expert review of flagged robustness cases.

sections.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
sections.abstract: Reframes chain-of-thought controllability as a self-instruction problem and reports that self-reminders improve constraint-following, while also demonstrating a possible monitor-evasion risk.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Self-Instructed CoT Controllability and report higher controllability than with user-prompt constraints; they also show a monitoring setup in which the capability can be used to evade a monitor.
sections.unique_caveat: Findings concern tested constraint and monitoring setups; they do not establish how often deployed systems can evade diverse monitors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Spans AI, language, and machine learning, includes code and data, and tests the connection between reasoning control and oversight.

sections.title: Not All Test-Time Compute Is Evidence: Model-Specific Bias in LLM Reasoning
sections.abstract: Argues that repeated samples and self-evaluations from one model have correlated errors, and proposes disagreement-triggered independent arbitration using heterogeneous solvers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report DIA outperforming full chain-of-thought in 12 of 14 settings, including a 7.00% gain on MuSiQue, while activating on about 17% of examples and using up to 47.2% fewer tokens than a multi-agent baseline.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation covers two base models and seven benchmarks; reported gains do not show that heterogeneous arbitration is better for every task or model family.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports results over seven benchmarks and two base models, comparing against full chain-of-thought and a multi-agent baseline.

sections.title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
sections.abstract: Introduces a post-hoc video refinement model trained on synthetic paired data to correct geometric inconsistency under camera motion, reporting improvements on pose-conditioned and prompt-driven benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Video Geometry Corrector and VG-Pairs, using synthetic paired supervision and optical flow to improve geometry without changing the source video generator.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports benchmark results with synthetic supervision; it does not establish performance on all real-world camera-motion distributions or subjective video quality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026 and evaluated across multiple source generators and two benchmark types.

sections.title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
sections.abstract: Introduces Consistent Sparse Dictionary Learning, replacing a standard linear encoder with per-sample sparse coding to improve consistency of learned feature dictionaries across training runs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report near-perfect dictionary and coefficient recovery across 16 synthetic settings and improvements of 17.6% and 35.9% in dictionary and coefficient consistency over six SAE baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract supports results in the specified synthetic and four applied settings; it does not show that learned features are universally more semantically meaningful or causally faithful.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports synthetic recovery tests and cross-seed consistency tests in four vision/language settings, targeting reproducibility in interpretability methods.

sections.title: GOLD: Geometric Optimized Latent Diffusion for Structure-Aware RNA Inverse Folding
sections.abstract: Presents a unified latent-diffusion approach for RNA sequence and side-chain geometry generation, with gradient-guided sampling to encourage physically stable structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce GeoVAE for sequence/geometry co-diffusion and a training-free gradient-guidance step; they report state-of-the-art results on the listed computational metrics.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported evidence is computational structural evaluation; therapeutic usefulness or experimental wet-lab validation is not established by the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted as a NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight paper, with evaluations on sequence recovery, secondary-structure validity, and 3D foldability; available Semantic Scholar record showed zero citations at snapshot time.
